devops-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — production cont-batching path p99 spike detected for streaming workloads. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/1919753100 :rotating_light:

alex: saw it — p95 ~ 220ms -> 420ms, p99 jumped to ~2.4s over last 6m. Streaming stalls reported by multiple customers.

maya: confirmed, looks correlated with mixed sequence-length traffic surge from a few tenants. Queue depth on cont-batch scheduler increasing.

priya: throwing logs here: `scheduler: enqueue_time_ms=120, dequeue_time_ms=1850, batch_size=128` repeated. KV cache eviction rate spiked at the same time.

sam: any recent deploys to the batching scheduler or kernel selection?

alex: no infra deploys in last 12h. We did push a new quantized LLM variant to the staging catalog but not routed.

maya: attaching flamegraph snapshot (copied compressed) — long tail inside batching selection loop when requests with seqlen > 1024 intermingle with short ones. Fairness heuristic seems to starve short-request lanes while waiting to fill large batches.

priya: interesting — continuous batching currently uses a single global bucket with dynamic padding. Mixed seqlen means batches pad to long lengths, increasing token compute and KV cache churn. That's likely why KV evictions and dequeue stalls happened.

sam: action ideas: 1) reduce max_batch_size for streaming route, 2) split buckets by seqlen (short/long), 3) temporarily disable cont-batching for streaming, 4) enable preemptive scheduling (fairshare) to avoid starvation. Which do we want first?

alex: short-term mitigation: reduce `max_batch_size` to 32 for streaming route and enable fairshare preemption. That should cut worst-case padding and let short requests go through quickly.

maya: +1. I can push a config patch to the routing layer. Command: ```curl -X POST "https://control-plane.internal/configs/batching" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"/stream","max_batch_size":32,"scheduler":"fairshare_preempt"}'```

priya: I'll standby to toggle cont-batching off for `/stream` if latency doesn't drop in 5m. Command to flip: `rbctl route update --name stream --cont_batching=false`

oncall-bot: Paging maya (primary oncall), priya (secondary). Incident severity: S1 (customer-impacting latency).

maya: applying the `max_batch_size=32` and `fairshare_preempt` now. Patching... `PATCH /configs/batching 200 OK`

alex: metrics starting to move: p95 -> 260ms, p99 -> 650ms (down from 2.4s). Good signal.

priya: KV eviction rate trending down, however we still see occasional 1.2s stalls on long sequences. Might need bucket splitting for full fix.

sam: can we do bucket split without a heavy rollout? Maybe shadow split first.

maya: I can create a two-bucket policy: seqlen <= 256 -> short, 257-2048 -> long. Shadow route will classify but not change routing. If that helps we can flip live.

alex: if shadow shows correctness within 10m, flip to active. Priya, Sam please monitor customer error rates and streaming stall traces.

priya: running traces: tracer id=trace-1919753, showing most stalls originate from combos where long requests join batches just before flush. We should also reduce `batch_wait_ms` for short bucket to reduce head-of-line blocking.

maya: shadow policy applied. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/cont-batch-shadow/1919753100

sam: also adding a conservative KV cache TTL bump for batch contexts to reduce churn: `kvctl set ttl --key-prefix=batch_ctx --ttl=120s` — applied.

alex: current numbers 8m after mitigation: p95=240ms, p99=420ms, queue depth normalized. Customer support ticket count flattened.

priya: recommend follow-ups: 1) permanent two-bucket split with independent max_batch sizes, 2) add sequence-length aware kernel selection to avoid overpadding, 3) unit tests / chaos tests around mixed seqlen workloads, 4) post-incident retrospective on scheduler fairness.

sam: logging TODOs: add a `batch_reason` tag in traces (why batch flushed — timeout, capacity, seqlen) and export per-route histogram of pad overhead.

maya: agreed. I'll open an RFC for the two-bucket change with perf sims and rollout plan.

oncall-bot: Handoff reminder: maya -> priya at 2026-03-15 08:15 UTC.

alex: for the handoff notes to next oncall (Priya): Current state: spike mitigated via `max_batch_size=32` + `fairshare_preempt` + KV TTL bump. Shadow two-bucket policy in place and looks promising. Monitor p99 < 500ms, keep `cont-batching` off for `/stream` if it regresses.

priya: ack, taking over. Will keep an eye for 2h, will flip buckets active after smoke tests pass. If p99 > 700ms, rollback to old config and escalate.

sam: leaving a quick postmortem template TODO in #postmortems.

alex: thanks all. Incident status -> mitigating. Will update ticket and create follow-up items.

priya: handed off and closing active paging loop for now. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Incident state changed: mitigating -> monitoring.
